title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning Weight Refit with the Reshard Collective | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA introduces the Reshard collective (open-source NCCL M2N Reshard) that recasts RL post-training weight refit as a DTensor-to-DTensor transfer moving only the minimum data, replacing gather-and-broadcast that would move ~10 TB per step for trillion-parameter models. In NeMo RL it cut refit latency 2.7-5.7x on DGX H100 and GB200, and refit a 2.4T-parameter model in 4.3 s.

themes.theme: RL refit as a scaling bottleneck

insights.claim: In disaggregated RL post-training, inference (rollout) and training run on separate GPUs, so updated policy weights must be periodically transferred to the inference GPUs, a step called refit.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: RL post-training creates a new, communication-heavy workload pattern that drives demand for high-bandwidth interconnect.
insights.quote: This transfer of model weights between training and inference GPUs is called refit.

insights.claim: Refit is hard because training and inference use different parallel mappings (data, context, tensor, expert, pipeline) and the payload is on the order of the model's full weight size.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Mismatched layouts plus full-model payloads make refit a structural cost that grows with frontier model size.

insights.claim: Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters (~5.6 TB in BF16) and Qwen 3.8 2.4T A95B has 2.4 trillion (~4.8 TB), implying gather-and-broadcast refit payloads of about 11.2 TB and 9.6 TB respectively.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight models now sit at multi-trillion-parameter scale, setting the size frontier NVIDIA is engineering for.
insights.quote: Kimi K3 contains 2.8 trillion parameters, while Qwen 3.8 2.4T A95B contains 2.4 trillion parameters
insights.locator: The size of this communication grows

insights.claim: For today's largest open-weight models, refit communication already reaches around 10 TB and must be performed at every training step, and the overhead will grow as LLMs scale.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Per-step multi-terabyte transfers make networking (NVLink, InfiniBand/Ethernet) a first-order constraint on RL training throughput.
insights.quote: the communication payload already reaches around 10 TB per refit, which must be performed at every training step
insights.locator: For today’s largest open weight models

insights.claim: Conventional gather-and-broadcast refit is wasteful because every inference GPU receives the full parameter even when it only needs a shard, creating redundant traffic in both phases.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Software inefficiency in RL pipelines is large, so communication algorithms can unlock big utilization gains on existing clusters.
insights.quote: an inference GPU receives the full parameter even when it needs only a shard
insights.locator: Using the complete tensor as an intermediate

insights.claim: NVIDIA reformulates weight refit as resharding a PyTorch DTensor from the training layout to the inference layout, so only the theoretical minimum data moves regardless of either side's parallelism configuration.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Building on PyTorch's DTensor abstraction eases ecosystem adoption while routing the hot path through NVIDIA's NCCL.
insights.quote: weight refit can be reformulated as resharding a DTensor from the training layout to the inference layout
insights.locator: The key to addressing this challenge

insights.claim: Reshard is proposed as a new first-class collective alongside all-reduce, all-gather and broadcast, specified only by source and destination DTensor descriptions so algorithms can improve inside the library independent of applications.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Defining a new collective primitive extends NCCL's role as the standard comms layer and makes NVIDIA's library the place where RL infra improvements accrue.
insights.quote: Reshard is a new type of collective communication call for arbitrary DTensor-to-DTensor transfers.

insights.claim: NCCL M2N Reshard, the open-source reference implementation on GitHub (NVIDIA/nccl-extensions), moves a tensor from M source GPUs to the layout required by N destination GPUs.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing keeps frameworks on NCCL rather than custom transport, reinforcing NVIDIA's software moat.
insights.locator: NCCL M2N Reshard is open source

insights.claim: NCCL M2N Reshard derives exact shard intersections, then groups destination replicas by NVLink domain so each source shard crosses the network once and replicas exchange the remainder over NVLink, pipelined with network transfer.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: The design converts scarce scale-out network bandwidth into cheaper NVLink bandwidth, strengthening the value of large NVLink domains like NVL72.
insights.quote: groups replicas by NVIDIA NVLink domain
insights.locator: How NCCL M2N Reshard unlocks maximum network bandwidth

insights.claim: With naive point-to-point transfer to two DP replicas, each shard is sent twice and gets roughly half the network bandwidth; Reshard sends it once so each shard gets the full network bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Eliminating replica duplication effectively doubles usable network bandwidth for refit in common layouts.
insights.quote: This way, each shard gets the full network bandwidth.
insights.locator: NCCL M2N Reshard transfers each source shard

insights.claim: Feed-forward projection weights account for around 95% of parameters in the latest LLMs, so NeMo RL routes them through Reshard while small weights (QKV, Mamba) keep the gather-and-broadcast path for coverage.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: A pragmatic 95/5 split shows production RL infra prioritizes the dominant payload; MoE/FFN-heavy architectures maximize the benefit.
insights.quote: these weights account for around 95% of the model’s parameters
insights.locator: To develop an efficient and sustainable design

insights.claim: The variety of layer types and inconsistent sharding across training and inference engines make it hard to cover every edge case with the Reshard collective alone.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Fragmentation between training and inference engines remains a real integration tax, limiting plug-and-play adoption.

insights.claim: NeMo RL currently handles GPU membership changes during failure recovery by destroying and recreating the communicator group, with NCCL shrink and grow APIs planned for future resiliency support.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Elastic, fault-tolerant RL training at scale is still maturing; resiliency features are on the roadmap.
insights.quote: Resiliency support using NCCL shrink and grow APIs is planned for future updates.
insights.locator: The sharding layout can change at runtime

insights.claim: In NeMo RL benchmarks on DGX H100 (NVL8) and DGX GB200 (NVL72), Reshard refit was 2.7x to 5.7x faster than gather-and-broadcast refit.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Multi-x refit speedups raise GPU utilization in RL post-training, improving the economics of reasoning-model training.
insights.quote: the reshard refit achieves a speedup of 2.7x to 5.7x over conventional gather-and-broadcast refit
insights.locator: RL weight refit performance benchmark results

insights.claim: For DeepSeek v3 671B, refit latency dropped from 14.9 s to 2.6 s on DGX H100 but from 6.1 s to 2.3 s on DGX GB200, meaning GB200's larger NVLink domain already made the baseline about 2.4x faster.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: GB200 NVL72 delivers structural RL refit advantages over H100 even before software fixes, supporting the upgrade case.
insights.locator: Table 2. Refit latencies measured in NeMo RL

insights.claim: Reshard refit cut Qwen 3 235B refit on DGX H100 from 6.4 s to 1.9 s and Nemotron Ultra v3 on DGX GB200 from 8.2 s to 2.3 s.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Seconds saved per step compound across thousands of RL steps, cutting idle GPU time on both training and inference pools.
insights.locator: Table 2. Refit latencies measured in NeMo RL

insights.claim: In a refit-only microbenchmark, Reshard refit took only 4.3 seconds for the 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8 2.4T BF16 model.
insights.speaker: Youngeun Kwon
insights.so_what: Seconds-scale refit at trillion-parameter scale removes a barrier to RL post-training of the next generation of giant models.
insights.quote: Reshard refit took only 4.3 seconds for the Qwen3.8 2.4T BF16 model
